steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths of visible light — particularly blue light — are scattered much more efficiently than longer wavelengths like red and orange, sending blue light in all directions across the sky. When you look at any part of the sky (away from the sun), your eyes receive this scattered blue light, making the entire sky appear blue.
